Clean. The workspace now contains only the source changes (no build artifacts), and the build/runtime verification confirmed everything works correctly.

## Summary

The core issue: this SaaS pivoted from **InboxZap** (email cleanup) to **Lumina** (AI meeting assistant), but the codebase never caught up — it was quietly bleeding the only organic traffic it had while giving the new product nothing to rank on. Fixes made:

**Technical debt (was actively blocking indexing/crawling):**
- `app/layout.tsx` had hardcoded InboxZap title/description/OG tags site-wide, contradicting every page's actual content — fixed with correct Lumina metadata, title template, and Organization schema.
- Nav/footer linked to `/features` and `/pricing`, which didn't exist in the repo (404s) — built both out.
- `/faq` permanently redirected to `/#faq`, an anchor that existed nowhere — built a real `/faq` page with `FAQPage` schema instead.
- The blog fetched posts from `/api/posts`, which doesn't exist — Google and users got an infinite "Loading posts…" spinner with zero links. Rewrote it as fully static-generated pages (`generateStaticParams`/`generateMetadata`, `BlogPosting` schema).
- `sitemap.ts` only listed 4 static URLs and never included any blog post — now includes everything.

**Content strategy (the actual traffic problem):**
- All 12 existing blog posts and 100% of GSC query data were about email/Gmail/Outlook cleanup — completely irrelevant to a meeting-assistant product, and already converting at near-0% CTR. 301-redirected them to `/blog` rather than let already-indexed URLs 404 or keep diluting topical relevance.
- Replaced them with 5 new posts actually targeting Lumina's ICP (meeting notes templates, action items, async standups, AI summary accuracy), each linking back to `/features`/`/pricing`.
- One deliberate bridge post, *"Meeting Overload Is Flooding Your Inbox"*, legitimately connects the old high-impression "email overload" query demand to the new product.
- Added a one-line rebrand note on the homepage plus a dedicated FAQ answer ("What happened to InboxZap?") so the ~18 clicks/month of existing brand-search traffic for "inboxzap" lands somewhere coherent instead of bouncing off an unrelated product page.

Verified with a real `npm run build` + `npm start`: all routes 200, redirects fire correctly, sitemap is complete, titles match page content.
